Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer/hanging man, inverted hammer/shooting star, doji incl. dragonfly/gravestone, morning/evening star, piercing/dark cloud, three soldiers/crows, inside/outside bar, harami) scanned on the last 5 bars of each timeframe; bias requires the prior 10-bar trend (e.g. hammer only after a decline); confirmed = bar volume >= 1.2x its average (same time-of-day slot over prior sessions on 5m/15m/1h, else 20-bar); context = within 0.6 ATR of that timeframe's S/R, order block or Fibonacci-at-S/R level. Intraday bars filtered to regular hours (9:30-16:00 ET); bars under 5% of 20-bar avg volume skipped. Volume study per timeframe: 20-bar average, last-bar multiple, up/down volume ratio, OBV slope, climax flag (>= 2.5x).

Wyckoff phases are hypotheses, not conclusions: a rule-based label (50-bar MA slope, 60-bar range position, up/down volume) is tested against the volume story (up/down ratio, OBV slope, climaxes, volume on confirmed candles), context (position in the 52-week/long range, trend leading into the range, springs/upthrusts/signs of strength or weakness at the range edges, reactions at S/R, order blocks, Fibonacci and options walls, gap/news distortion) and the higher timeframe (1d vs 1w, 4h/1h vs 1d). Disagreements are listed as conflicts with both readings and lower confidence; low-confidence labels are treated as neutral.

Big picture: every study is treated as contextual evidence, not a standalone trigger. Per timeframe, trend (MACD + Bollinger), RSI, Wyckoff hypothesis (neutral if low confidence), volume (OBV, up/down) and confirmed candles each vote; timeframes are weighted 1w/1d 3, 4h/1h 2, 15m/5m 1. Agreement, cross-timeframe conflicts and data that does not fit (RSI divergence, breakouts on weak volume, candles against the trend, contested Wyckoff, price vs options walls/gamma flip) (each weighted by its misfit-outcome track record once the sample is large enough) set confidence, odds and suggested size (high = full, medium = ~2/3, low = ~1/3 or wait). The recommended ladder itself is unchanged.

Misfit learning: every misfit, disagreement and Wyckoff conflict is logged with price, thesis bias and context, then resolved after 5 sessions (daily/weekly) or 1 session (intraday) as warned correctly, supported the study, noise (move < half an expected range) or news distortion (gap > 1.5 ATR). A scorecard by type (bootstrapped from 2-year daily history) sets how much each type lowers confidence once it has 8+ cases; see "What misfits mean" in the playbook.

Anomaly loop: each run checks the last 20 sessions and the live snapshot for price against studies/options, news-vs-price inversions, up moves on falling volume, unusual range/volume (incl. time-of-day), gaps, decoupling from SPY/QQQ/SMH, IV/skew shifts vs price and repeated failures at S/R. Each gets expected vs actual and a candidate explanation (sector/market move, Alpaca news); unexplained ones are revisited at +5 and +20 sessions and classified as a recognizable pattern, noise or still developing. Learned patterns ("Anomaly patterns" in the playbook) are matched on later runs and feed the picture; recent anomalies (last 10 days) add to the confidence load. No earnings/macro calendar or spread history is connected yet.

Per-pull learning: every run compares fresh data with the stock profile (2y level tests/holds/breaks, typical pullbacks and reaction sizes, volume habits, gap fills, options-wall respect) and logs what is new, contradicting, repeating or surprising to the learning log; the profile compounds across pulls.

Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer/hanging man, inverted hammer/shooting star, doji incl. dragonfly/gravestone, morning/evening star, piercing/dark cloud, three soldiers/crows, inside/outside bar, harami) scanned on the last 5 bars of each timeframe; bias requires the prior 10-bar trend (e.g. hammer only after a decline); confirmed = bar volume >= 1.2x its average (same time-of-day slot over prior sessions on 5m/15m/1h, else 20-bar); context = within 0.6 ATR of that timeframe's S/R, order block or Fibonacci-at-S/R level. Intraday bars filtered to regular hours (9:30-16:00 ET); bars under 5% of 20-bar avg volume skipped. Volume study per timeframe: 20-bar average, last-bar multiple, up/down volume ratio, OBV slope, climax flag (>= 2.5x).

Wyckoff phases are hypotheses, not conclusions: a rule-based label (50-bar MA slope, 60-bar range position, up/down volume) is tested against the volume story (up/down ratio, OBV slope, climaxes, volume on confirmed candles), context (position in the 52-week/long range, trend leading into the range, springs/upthrusts/signs of strength or weakness at the range edges, reactions at S/R, order blocks, Fibonacci and options walls, gap/news distortion) and the higher timeframe (1d vs 1w, 4h/1h vs 1d). Disagreements are listed as conflicts with both readings and lower confidence; low-confidence labels are treated as neutral.

Big picture: every study is treated as contextual evidence, not a standalone trigger. Per timeframe, trend (MACD + Bollinger), RSI, Wyckoff hypothesis (neutral if low confidence), volume (OBV, up/down) and confirmed candles each vote; timeframes are weighted 1w/1d 3, 4h/1h 2, 15m/5m 1. Agreement, cross-timeframe conflicts and data that does not fit (RSI divergence, breakouts on weak volume, candles against the trend, contested Wyckoff, price vs options walls/gamma flip) (each weighted by its misfit-outcome track record once the sample is large enough) set confidence, odds and suggested size (high = full, medium = ~2/3, low = ~1/3 or wait). The recommended ladder itself is unchanged.

Misfit learning: every misfit, disagreement and Wyckoff conflict is logged with price, thesis bias and context, then resolved after 5 sessions (daily/weekly) or 1 session (intraday) as warned correctly, supported the study, noise (move < half an expected range) or news distortion (gap > 1.5 ATR). A scorecard by type (bootstrapped from 2-year daily history) sets how much each type lowers confidence once it has 8+ cases; see "What misfits mean" in the playbook.

Anomaly loop: each run checks the last 20 sessions and the live snapshot for price against studies/options, news-vs-price inversions, up moves on falling volume, unusual range/volume (incl. time-of-day), gaps, decoupling from SPY/QQQ/SMH, IV/skew shifts vs price and repeated failures at S/R. Each gets expected vs actual and a candidate explanation (sector/market move, Alpaca news); unexplained ones are revisited at +5 and +20 sessions and classified as a recognizable pattern, noise or still developing. Learned patterns ("Anomaly patterns" in the playbook) are matched on later runs and feed the picture; recent anomalies (last 10 days) add to the confidence load. No earnings/macro calendar or spread history is connected yet.

Per-pull learning: every run compares fresh data with the stock profile (2y level tests/holds/breaks, typical pullbacks and reaction sizes, volume habits, gap fills, options-wall respect) and logs what is new, contradicting, repeating or surprising to the learning log; the profile compounds across pulls.

Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer/hanging man, inverted hammer/shooting star, doji incl. dragonfly/gravestone, morning/evening star, piercing/dark cloud, three soldiers/crows, inside/outside bar, harami) scanned on the last 5 bars of each timeframe; bias requires the prior 10-bar trend (e.g. hammer only after a decline); confirmed = bar volume >= 1.2x its average (same time-of-day slot over prior sessions on 5m/15m/1h, else 20-bar); context = within 0.6 ATR of that timeframe's S/R, order block or Fibonacci-at-S/R level. Intraday bars filtered to regular hours (9:30-16:00 ET); bars under 5% of 20-bar avg volume skipped. Volume study per timeframe: 20-bar average, last-bar multiple, up/down volume ratio, OBV slope, climax flag (>= 2.5x).

Wyckoff phases are hypotheses, not conclusions: a rule-based label (50-bar MA slope, 60-bar range position, up/down volume) is tested against the volume story (up/down ratio, OBV slope, climaxes, volume on confirmed candles), context (position in the 52-week/long range, trend leading into the range, springs/upthrusts/signs of strength or weakness at the range edges, reactions at S/R, order blocks, Fibonacci and options walls, gap/news distortion) and the higher timeframe (1d vs 1w, 4h/1h vs 1d). Disagreements are listed as conflicts with both readings and lower confidence; low-confidence labels are treated as neutral.

Big picture: every study is treated as contextual evidence, not a standalone trigger. Per timeframe, trend (MACD + Bollinger), RSI, Wyckoff hypothesis (neutral if low confidence), volume (OBV, up/down) and confirmed candles each vote; timeframes are weighted 1w/1d 3, 4h/1h 2, 15m/5m 1. Agreement, cross-timeframe conflicts and data that does not fit (RSI divergence, breakouts on weak volume, candles against the trend, contested Wyckoff, price vs options walls/gamma flip) (each weighted by its misfit-outcome track record once the sample is large enough) set confidence, odds and suggested size (high = full, medium = ~2/3, low = ~1/3 or wait). The recommended ladder itself is unchanged.

Misfit learning: every misfit, disagreement and Wyckoff conflict is logged with price, thesis bias and context, then resolved after 5 sessions (daily/weekly) or 1 session (intraday) as warned correctly, supported the study, noise (move < half an expected range) or news distortion (gap > 1.5 ATR). A scorecard by type (bootstrapped from 2-year daily history) sets how much each type lowers confidence once it has 8+ cases; see "What misfits mean" in the playbook.

Anomaly loop: each run checks the last 20 sessions and the live snapshot for price against studies/options, news-vs-price inversions, up moves on falling volume, unusual range/volume (incl. time-of-day), gaps, decoupling from SPY/QQQ/SMH, IV/skew shifts vs price and repeated failures at S/R. Each gets expected vs actual and a candidate explanation (sector/market move, Alpaca news); unexplained ones are revisited at +5 and +20 sessions and classified as a recognizable pattern, noise or still developing. Learned patterns ("Anomaly patterns" in the playbook) are matched on later runs and feed the picture; recent anomalies (last 10 days) add to the confidence load. No earnings/macro calendar or spread history is connected yet.

Per-pull learning: every run compares fresh data with the stock profile (2y level tests/holds/breaks, typical pullbacks and reaction sizes, volume habits, gap fills, options-wall respect) and logs what is new, contradicting, repeating or surprising to the learning log; the profile compounds across pulls.

Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer/hanging man, inverted hammer/shooting star, doji incl. dragonfly/gravestone, morning/evening star, piercing/dark cloud, three soldiers/crows, inside/outside bar, harami) scanned on the last 5 bars of each timeframe; bias requires the prior 10-bar trend (e.g. hammer only after a decline); confirmed = bar volume >= 1.2x its average (same time-of-day slot over prior sessions on 5m/15m/1h, else 20-bar); context = within 0.6 ATR of that timeframe's S/R, order block or Fibonacci-at-S/R level. Intraday bars filtered to regular hours (9:30-16:00 ET); bars under 5% of 20-bar avg volume skipped. Volume study per timeframe: 20-bar average, last-bar multiple, up/down volume ratio, OBV slope, climax flag (>= 2.5x).

Wyckoff phases are hypotheses, not conclusions: a rule-based label (50-bar MA slope, 60-bar range position, up/down volume) is tested against the volume story (up/down ratio, OBV slope, climaxes, volume on confirmed candles), context (position in the 52-week/long range, trend leading into the range, springs/upthrusts/signs of strength or weakness at the range edges, reactions at S/R, order blocks, Fibonacci and options walls, gap/news distortion) and the higher timeframe (1d vs 1w, 4h/1h vs 1d). Disagreements are listed as conflicts with both readings and lower confidence; low-confidence labels are treated as neutral.

Big picture: every study is treated as contextual evidence, not a standalone trigger. Per timeframe, trend (MACD + Bollinger), RSI, Wyckoff hypothesis (neutral if low confidence), volume (OBV, up/down) and confirmed candles each vote; timeframes are weighted 1w/1d 3, 4h/1h 2, 15m/5m 1. Agreement, cross-timeframe conflicts and data that does not fit (RSI divergence, breakouts on weak volume, candles against the trend, contested Wyckoff, price vs options walls/gamma flip) (each weighted by its misfit-outcome track record once the sample is large enough) set confidence, odds and suggested size (high = full, medium = ~2/3, low = ~1/3 or wait). The recommended ladder itself is unchanged.

Misfit learning: every misfit, disagreement and Wyckoff conflict is logged with price, thesis bias and context, then resolved after 5 sessions (daily/weekly) or 1 session (intraday) as warned correctly, supported the study, noise (move < half an expected range) or news distortion (gap > 1.5 ATR). A scorecard by type (bootstrapped from 2-year daily history) sets how much each type lowers confidence once it has 8+ cases; see "What misfits mean" in the playbook.

Anomaly loop: each run checks the last 20 sessions and the live snapshot for price against studies/options, news-vs-price inversions, up moves on falling volume, unusual range/volume (incl. time-of-day), gaps, decoupling from SPY/QQQ/SMH, IV/skew shifts vs price and repeated failures at S/R. Each gets expected vs actual and a candidate explanation (sector/market move, Alpaca news); unexplained ones are revisited at +5 and +20 sessions and classified as a recognizable pattern, noise or still developing. Learned patterns ("Anomaly patterns" in the playbook) are matched on later runs and feed the picture; recent anomalies (last 10 days) add to the confidence load. No earnings/macro calendar or spread history is connected yet.

Per-pull learning: every run compares fresh data with the stock profile (2y level tests/holds/breaks, typical pullbacks and reaction sizes, volume habits, gap fills, options-wall respect) and logs what is new, contradicting, repeating or surprising to the learning log; the profile compounds across pulls.

Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer/hanging man, inverted hammer/shooting star, doji incl. dragonfly/gravestone, morning/evening star, piercing/dark cloud, three soldiers/crows, inside/outside bar, harami) scanned on the last 5 bars of each timeframe; bias requires the prior 10-bar trend (e.g. hammer only after a decline); confirmed = bar volume >= 1.2x its average (same time-of-day slot over prior sessions on 5m/15m/1h, else 20-bar); context = within 0.6 ATR of that timeframe's S/R, order block or Fibonacci-at-S/R level. Intraday bars filtered to regular hours (9:30-16:00 ET); bars under 5% of 20-bar avg volume skipped. Volume study per timeframe: 20-bar average, last-bar multiple, up/down volume ratio, OBV slope, climax flag (>= 2.5x).

Wyckoff phases are hypotheses, not conclusions: a rule-based label (50-bar MA slope, 60-bar range position, up/down volume) is tested against the volume story (up/down ratio, OBV slope, climaxes, volume on confirmed candles), context (position in the 52-week/long range, trend leading into the range, springs/upthrusts/signs of strength or weakness at the range edges, reactions at S/R, order blocks, Fibonacci and options walls, gap/news distortion) and the higher timeframe (1d vs 1w, 4h/1h vs 1d). Disagreements are listed as conflicts with both readings and lower confidence; low-confidence labels are treated as neutral.

Big picture: every study is treated as contextual evidence, not a standalone trigger. Per timeframe, trend (MACD + Bollinger), RSI, Wyckoff hypothesis (neutral if low confidence), volume (OBV, up/down) and confirmed candles each vote; timeframes are weighted 1w/1d 3, 4h/1h 2, 15m/5m 1. Agreement, cross-timeframe conflicts and data that does not fit (RSI divergence, breakouts on weak volume, candles against the trend, contested Wyckoff, price vs options walls/gamma flip) (each weighted by its misfit-outcome track record once the sample is large enough) set confidence, odds and suggested size (high = full, medium = ~2/3, low = ~1/3 or wait). The recommended ladder itself is unchanged.

Misfit learning: every misfit, disagreement and Wyckoff conflict is logged with price, thesis bias and context, then resolved after 5 sessions (daily/weekly) or 1 session (intraday) as warned correctly, supported the study, noise (move < half an expected range) or news distortion (gap > 1.5 ATR). A scorecard by type (bootstrapped from 2-year daily history) sets how much each type lowers confidence once it has 8+ cases; see "What misfits mean" in the playbook.

Anomaly loop: each run checks the last 20 sessions and the live snapshot for price against studies/options, news-vs-price inversions, up moves on falling volume, unusual range/volume (incl. time-of-day), gaps, decoupling from SPY/QQQ/SMH, IV/skew shifts vs price and repeated failures at S/R. Each gets expected vs actual and a candidate explanation (sector/market move, Alpaca news); unexplained ones are revisited at +5 and +20 sessions and classified as a recognizable pattern, noise or still developing. Learned patterns ("Anomaly patterns" in the playbook) are matched on later runs and feed the picture; recent anomalies (last 10 days) add to the confidence load. No earnings/macro calendar or spread history is connected yet.

Per-pull learning: every run compares fresh data with the stock profile (2y level tests/holds/breaks, typical pullbacks and reaction sizes, volume habits, gap fills, options-wall respect) and logs what is new, contradicting, repeating or surprising to the learning log; the profile compounds across pulls.

Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer/hanging man, inverted hammer/shooting star, doji incl. dragonfly/gravestone, morning/evening star, piercing/dark cloud, three soldiers/crows, inside/outside bar, harami) scanned on the last 5 bars of each timeframe; bias requires the prior 10-bar trend (e.g. hammer only after a decline); confirmed = bar volume >= 1.2x its average (same time-of-day slot over prior sessions on 5m/15m/1h, else 20-bar); context = within 0.6 ATR of that timeframe's S/R, order block or Fibonacci-at-S/R level. Intraday bars filtered to regular hours (9:30-16:00 ET); bars under 5% of 20-bar avg volume skipped. Volume study per timeframe: 20-bar average, last-bar multiple, up/down volume ratio, OBV slope, climax flag (>= 2.5x).

Wyckoff phases are hypotheses, not conclusions: a rule-based label (50-bar MA slope, 60-bar range position, up/down volume) is tested against the volume story (up/down ratio, OBV slope, climaxes, volume on confirmed candles), context (position in the 52-week/long range, trend leading into the range, springs/upthrusts/signs of strength or weakness at the range edges, reactions at S/R, order blocks, Fibonacci and options walls, gap/news distortion) and the higher timeframe (1d vs 1w, 4h/1h vs 1d). Disagreements are listed as conflicts with both readings and lower confidence; low-confidence labels are treated as neutral.

Big picture: every study is treated as contextual evidence, not a standalone trigger. Per timeframe, trend (MACD + Bollinger), RSI, Wyckoff hypothesis (neutral if low confidence), volume (OBV, up/down) and confirmed candles each vote; timeframes are weighted 1w/1d 3, 4h/1h 2, 15m/5m 1. Agreement, cross-timeframe conflicts and data that does not fit (RSI divergence, breakouts on weak volume, candles against the trend, contested Wyckoff, price vs options walls/gamma flip) (each weighted by its misfit-outcome track record once the sample is large enough) set confidence, odds and suggested size (high = full, medium = ~2/3, low = ~1/3 or wait). The recommended ladder itself is unchanged.

Misfit learning: every misfit, disagreement and Wyckoff conflict is logged with price, thesis bias and context, then resolved after 5 sessions (daily/weekly) or 1 session (intraday) as warned correctly, supported the study, noise (move < half an expected range) or news distortion (gap > 1.5 ATR). A scorecard by type (bootstrapped from 2-year daily history) sets how much each type lowers confidence once it has 8+ cases; see "What misfits mean" in the playbook.

Anomaly loop: each run checks the last 20 sessions and the live snapshot for price against studies/options, news-vs-price inversions, up moves on falling volume, unusual range/volume (incl. time-of-day), gaps, decoupling from SPY/QQQ/SMH, IV/skew shifts vs price and repeated failures at S/R. Each gets expected vs actual and a candidate explanation (sector/market move, Alpaca news); unexplained ones are revisited at +5 and +20 sessions and classified as a recognizable pattern, noise or still developing. Learned patterns ("Anomaly patterns" in the playbook) are matched on later runs and feed the picture; recent anomalies (last 10 days) add to the confidence load. No earnings/macro calendar or spread history is connected yet.

Per-pull learning: every run compares fresh data with the stock profile (2y level tests/holds/breaks, typical pullbacks and reaction sizes, volume habits, gap fills, options-wall respect) and logs what is new, contradicting, repeating or surprising to the learning log; the profile compounds across pulls.

Price history from the local bar cache (/workspace/tp_private/bars): 15 series, 22 bars fetched this run and 39,999 reused from earlier pulls (15 incremental). Only bars after the last cached bar are requested, plus the last 1-2 bars to correct the still-forming one; a split or adjustment mismatch refetches that series in full.
Cache currency (FCX, CNBC): last daily bar 2026-10-09, last 5m bar Oct 9 2:55 PM CT; latest quote session 2026-10-09.
Snapshot studies (RSI, MACD, Bollinger, VWAP, Fibonacci at S/R, order blocks, Wyckoff hypotheses, gamma/OI walls) from Alpaca at Oct 10 9:05 PM CT.
Cache currency (FCX): last cached bar 5m Oct 9 2:55 PM CT; 15m Oct 9 2:45 PM CT; 1h Oct 9 2:00 PM CT; 4h Oct 9 11:00 AM CT; 1d Oct 9; 1w week of Oct 5. Latest completed session 2026-10-09.
Close cross-check vs CNBC (flag >0.5%): ok FCX 2026-10-09 cached close $73.70 vs CNBC last close $73.69 (0.01%); ok FCX 2026-10-08 cached close $71.14 vs CNBC prior close $71.14 (0.00%).

Bar cache: 12 FCX bars fetched this run, 3,127 reused from earlier pulls across 15m, 1d, 1h, 1w, 4h, 5m (incremental); studies run on the cached series, each over its own lookback window. Source: Alpaca IEX.

Candlestick patterns (engulfing, hammer/hanging man, inverted hammer/shooting star, doji incl. dragonfly/gravestone, morning/evening star, piercing/dark cloud, three soldiers/crows, inside/outside bar, harami) scanned on the last 5 bars of each timeframe; bias requires the prior 10-bar trend (e.g. hammer only after a decline); confirmed = bar volume >= 1.2x its average (same time-of-day slot over prior sessions on 5m/15m/1h, else 20-bar); context = within 0.6 ATR of that timeframe's S/R, order block or Fibonacci-at-S/R level. Intraday bars filtered to regular hours (9:30-16:00 ET); bars under 5% of 20-bar avg volume skipped. Volume study per timeframe: 20-bar average, last-bar multiple, up/down volume ratio, OBV slope, climax flag (>= 2.5x).

Wyckoff phases are hypotheses, not conclusions: a rule-based label (50-bar MA slope, 60-bar range position, up/down volume) is tested against the volume story (up/down ratio, OBV slope, climaxes, volume on confirmed candles), context (position in the 52-week/long range, trend leading into the range, springs/upthrusts/signs of strength or weakness at the range edges, reactions at S/R, order blocks, Fibonacci and options walls, gap/news distortion) and the higher timeframe (1d vs 1w, 4h/1h vs 1d). Disagreements are listed as conflicts with both readings and lower confidence; low-confidence labels are treated as neutral.

Big picture: every study is treated as contextual evidence, not a standalone trigger. Per timeframe, trend (MACD + Bollinger), RSI, Wyckoff hypothesis (neutral if low confidence), volume (OBV, up/down) and confirmed candles each vote; timeframes are weighted 1w/1d 3, 4h/1h 2, 15m/5m 1. Agreement, cross-timeframe conflicts and data that does not fit (RSI divergence, breakouts on weak volume, candles against the trend, contested Wyckoff, price vs options walls/gamma flip) (each weighted by its misfit-outcome track record once the sample is large enough) set confidence, odds and suggested size (high = full, medium = ~2/3, low = ~1/3 or wait). The recommended ladder itself is unchanged.

Misfit learning: every misfit, disagreement and Wyckoff conflict is logged with price, thesis bias and context, then resolved after 5 sessions (daily/weekly) or 1 session (intraday) as warned correctly, supported the study, noise (move < half an expected range) or news distortion (gap > 1.5 ATR). A scorecard by type (bootstrapped from 2-year daily history) sets how much each type lowers confidence once it has 8+ cases; see "What misfits mean" in the playbook.

Anomaly loop: each run checks the last 20 sessions and the live snapshot for price against studies/options, news-vs-price inversions, up moves on falling volume, unusual range/volume (incl. time-of-day), gaps, decoupling from SPY/QQQ/SMH, IV/skew shifts vs price and repeated failures at S/R. Each gets expected vs actual and a candidate explanation (sector/market move, Alpaca news); unexplained ones are revisited at +5 and +20 sessions and classified as a recognizable pattern, noise or still developing. Learned patterns ("Anomaly patterns" in the playbook) are matched on later runs and feed the picture; recent anomalies (last 10 days) add to the confidence load. No earnings/macro calendar or spread history is connected yet.

Per-pull learning: every run compares fresh data with the stock profile (2y level tests/holds/breaks, typical pullbacks and reaction sizes, volume habits, gap fills, options-wall respect) and logs what is new, contradicting, repeating or surprising to the learning log; the profile compounds across pulls.
